definition: In computational linguistics the Yarowsky algorithm is an unsupervised learning algorithm for word sense disambiguation that uses the "one sense per collocation" and the "one sense per discourse" properties of human languages for word sense disambiguation.
details: From observation, words tend to exhibit only one sense in most given discourse and in a given collocation.
story: Think of a grammar teacher who never memorized a rule but can still tell you when a sentence sounds wrong. In plain words: In computational linguistics the Yarowsky algorithm is an unsupervised learning algorithm for word sense disambiguation that uses the "one sense per collocation" and the "one sense per discourse" properties of human languages for word sense disambiguation. Here is how it actually plays out: From observation, words tend to exhibit only one sense in most given discourse and in a given collocation. The machine learns to read between the lines by reading an impossible number of lines. That pattern-earned fluency is Yarowsky algorithm.
